commands.title: Commands
commands.prefixTip: All TTS commands start with !tts.
commands.expandTip: Select any command row below to show usage details.
commands.webDashboardTip: Broadcasters and viewers can also change settings in the WildcatTTS Web Dashboard.
commands.myvoiceTip: Viewers can set personal TTS preferences in the web dashboard with !myvoice in chat.

ttsStatus.name: !tts status
ttsStatus.description: Shows the current TTS status for the channel.
ttsStatus.notes: Shows engine state, mode, queue length, default voice, pitch, speed, emotion, and language boost settings.

ttsVoices.name: !tts voices
ttsVoices.description: Shows a link to the list of available TTS voices.

ttsLanguageslist.name: !tts languageslist
ttsLanguageslist.description: Shows a link to the list of available TTS language boost options.

ttsCommands.name:
!tts commands
(Alias: !tts help)
ttsCommands.description: Shows a link to the full list of !tts subcommands.

ttsPrefs.name:
!tts prefs
(Aliases: !tts preferences, !tts settings)
ttsPrefs.description: Sends a link to your personal TTS settings page.
ttsPrefs.feature1: Set your own voice, pitch, speed, emotion, and language for this channel.
ttsPrefs.feature2: Includes a Danger Zone where you can add yourself to the TTS ignore list. Only a moderator can remove you.
ttsPrefs.feature3: The bot posts the link in chat with the channel context loaded.

myvoice.name: !myvoice
myvoice.description: Sends a link to your personal TTS settings page (same as !tts prefs).
myvoice.notes: Same as !tts prefs. The bot posts the link in chat with the channel context loaded.

ttsOn.name:
!tts on
(Alias: !tts enable)
ttsOn.description: Starts the TTS engine. TTS speaks messages and events based on the active mode.

ttsOff.name:
!tts off
(Alias: !tts disable)
ttsOff.description: Stops the TTS engine completely. TTS will not speak messages or events.

ttsMode.name: !tts mode [all|command|bits_points_only]
ttsMode.description: Sets or shows the TTS mode.
ttsMode.commandDesc: (Only speaks commands and enabled events; default mode)
ttsMode.bitsPointsOnlyDesc: (Only speaks Bits cheers and Channel Point redemptions)
ttsMode.notes:
all: TTS speaks all chat messages (except ignored users) and enabled events, based on !tts permission.
command: TTS speaks only commands (such as !tts <message>) and enabled events. TTS ignores regular chat.
bits_points_only: TTS speaks only Bits cheers and Channel Point redemptions. TTS ignores regular chat and commands.

ttsPermission.name: !tts permission [everyone|all|subs|vip|mods]
ttsPermission.description: Sets whose chat messages and !tts messages TTS speaks.
ttsPermission.notes:
everyone or all: TTS speaks messages from all users (Default).
subs: TTS speaks messages from subscribers, VIPs, moderators, and the broadcaster.
vip: TTS speaks messages from VIPs, moderators, and the broadcaster.
mods: TTS speaks messages only from moderators and the broadcaster.
This setting also applies to !tts <message> in command mode. Cheers and Channel Point redemptions are paid for and are not affected.

ttsBits.name: !tts bits [on|off|min <amount>]
ttsBits.description: Controls whether the message attached to a cheer is read aloud, and sets the minimum Bits a cheer needs.
ttsBits.onDesc: on: Read cheer messages. This is the default.
ttsBits.offDesc: off: Do not read cheer messages. Has no effect in bits_points_only mode, which always reads them.
ttsBits.minDesc: min <amount>: Sets the minimum Bits a cheer needs for its message to be read (for example, min 100). The default is 1. Cheer messages are read in every mode and are not limited by !tts permission.

channelPointsTTS.name: Channel Points → TTS
channelPointsTTS.description: Create a custom Channel Point reward for viewers to send messages that TTS reads aloud.
channelPointsTTS.noteText: Configure this feature in the Web Dashboard under the Channel Points → TTS section.
channelPointsTTS.step1: Streamer Setup: Turn on the feature in the dashboard.
channelPointsTTS.step2: Reward Creation: The bot creates a custom Channel Point reward on your Twitch channel.
channelPointsTTS.step3: Viewer Redemption: Viewers redeem the reward with a message that TTS speaks.
channelPointsTTS.step4: Content Policy: Filter text with length limits, link blocking, and banned words.
channelPointsTTS.basicSettings: Basic Settings: Reward title, cost in points, prompt text, and queue settings.
channelPointsTTS.advancedSettings: Advanced Settings: Global cooldown, stream limit, and user limit.
channelPointsTTS.contentPolicy: Content Policy: Minimum and maximum message length, link blocking, and banned words.
channelPointsTTS.skipQueueDefault: Default Setting: This option is on by default for immediate TTS playback.
channelPointsTTS.skipQueueEnabled: When On: TTS plays redemptions immediately without adding them to your Twitch review queue.
channelPointsTTS.skipQueueDisabled: When Off: Redemptions wait in your Twitch dashboard for manual approval before TTS plays.
channelPointsTTS.skipQueueUseCase: Tip: Turn on for instant playback. Turn off for moderation review before audio plays.
channelPointsTTS.ttsModesText: Works with all TTS modes (All Messages, Commands Only, Bits/Points Only).
channelPointsTTS.requirementsText: Grant channel:manage:redemptions and channel:read:redemptions permissions during dashboard sign-in.

ttsPause.name: !tts pause
ttsPause.description: Pauses processing of the TTS queue.
ttsPause.notes: The bot adds new messages and events to the queue, but does not speak them until resumed.

ttsResume.name: !tts resume
ttsResume.description: Resumes processing of the TTS queue.

ttsClear.name: !tts clear
ttsClear.description: Removes all waiting messages and events from the TTS queue.
ttsClear.notes: This command removes messages from the queue. It does not stop audio that is playing or generating.

ttsStop.name: !tts stop
ttsStop.description: Stops active or generating TTS audio.
ttsStop.note1: If TTS is speaking or generating audio, this command stops the playback.
ttsStop.note2: Any user can stop a message that their own chat message triggered.
ttsStop.note3: Moderators and the broadcaster can stop all TTS audio.
ttsStop.permission: Everyone for their own messages, Moderator for others

ttsVoice.name: !tts voice <voice_id|reset>
ttsVoice.description: Sets your personal voice preference for your chat messages.
ttsVoice.notes: Use reset to use the channel default voice. Use !tts voices to get a list of voice IDs.

ttsEmotion.name: !tts emotion <emotion_name|reset|auto>
ttsEmotion.description: Sets your personal emotion preference for your chat messages.
ttsEmotion.notes: Valid emotions: neutral, happy, sad, angry, fearful, disgusted, surprised. Use reset for the channel default.

ttsLanguage.name:
!tts language <language|reset>
(Alias: !tts lang)
ttsLanguage.description: Sets your personal language boost preference for your chat messages.
ttsLanguage.notes: Language boost improves pronunciation for a language. Use reset or auto for the channel default. Use !tts languageslist to see all options.

ttsPitch.name: !tts pitch <value|reset>
ttsPitch.description: Sets your personal TTS pitch for your chat messages.
ttsPitch.notes: Value must be an integer from -12 to 12 (0 is default). Use reset for the channel default.

ttsSpeed.name: !tts speed <value|reset>
ttsSpeed.description: Sets your personal TTS speech speed for your chat messages.
ttsSpeed.notes: Value must be a number from 0.5 to 2.0 (1.0 is default). Use reset for the channel default.

ttsIgnore.name:
!tts ignore <username>
!tts ignore add <username>
ttsIgnore.descriptionUser: For any user: Add yourself to the TTS ignore list. TTS will not speak your messages.
ttsIgnore.descriptionMod: For moderators and broadcasters: Add a Twitch user to the channel TTS ignore list.
ttsIgnore.usageModNote: (if you are a moderator or broadcaster)
ttsIgnore.permission: Everyone (to add themselves), Moderator (to add others)

ttsIgnoreDel.name:
!tts ignore del <username>
(Aliases: delete, rem, remove)
ttsIgnoreDel.description: Removes a Twitch user from the channel TTS ignore list.

ttsIgnored.name: !tts ignored
ttsIgnored.description: Lists all users on the channel TTS ignore list.

ttsEvents.name: !tts events [on|off]
ttsEvents.description: Turns Twitch event announcements (such as subscriptions, cheers, and raids) on or off.

ttsDefaultvoice.name: !tts defaultvoice <voice_id|reset>
ttsDefaultvoice.description: Sets the default TTS voice for the channel.
ttsDefaultvoice.notes: Use reset for the system default. Use !tts voices to see available voice IDs.

ttsDefaultemotion.name: !tts defaultemotion <emotion_name|reset>
ttsDefaultemotion.description: Sets the default TTS emotion for the channel.
ttsDefaultemotion.notes: Valid emotions: neutral, happy, sad, angry, fearful, disgusted, surprised. Use reset for the system default (neutral).

ttsDefaultlanguage.name: !tts defaultlanguage <language|reset>
ttsDefaultlanguage.description: Sets the default TTS language boost for the channel.
ttsDefaultlanguage.notes: Use reset or auto for the system default. Use !tts languageslist to see available options.

ttsDefaultpitch.name: !tts defaultpitch <value|reset>
ttsDefaultpitch.description: Sets the default TTS pitch for the channel.
ttsDefaultpitch.notes: Value must be an integer from -12 to 12 (0 is default). Use reset for the system default (0).

ttsDefaultspeed.name: !tts defaultspeed <value|reset>
ttsDefaultspeed.description: Sets the default TTS speed for the channel.
ttsDefaultspeed.notes: Value must be a number from 0.5 to 2.0 (1.0 is default). Use reset for the system default (1.0).

ttsMessage.name: !tts <message>
ttsMessage.description: Adds the message to the TTS queue immediately. This command works in all and command modes. TTS uses your preferences (or channel defaults) for voice, pitch, speed, and emotion.

ttsEmote.name: !tts emote <emoteName>
ttsEmote.description: Views, clears, or sets cached emote descriptions for TTS.
ttsEmote.viewDesc: Show the current AI description for an emote.
ttsEmote.regenerateDesc: Clear the cached description so AI creates a new description on next use.
ttsEmote.setDesc: Set a custom description for a channel emote.
ttsEmote.notes: When an emote appears in chat for the first time, AI generates a text description. The bot caches descriptions permanently. Use this command to view, change, or regenerate emote descriptions.

usage.set: !tts emote set LUL = a person laughing

ttsEmote.regenerateNote: (clears cache; AI creates a new description on next use)
ttsEmote.setNote: (sets a custom description — channel emotes only)

ttsPronounce.name: !tts pronounce <word> = <how to say it>
ttsPronounce.description: Controls how TTS says a specific word or short form.

usage.test: !tts pronounce test ngl that was wild

ttsPronounce.addDesc: Add a word and the text that TTS speaks in its place. Your entry replaces a built-in entry with the same word.
ttsPronounce.removeDesc: Remove your entry. If a built-in entry has the same word, that built-in entry becomes active again.
ttsPronounce.offDesc: Stop a built-in entry. To start it again, use the remove sub-command.
ttsPronounce.testDesc: Show what TTS will say for some text. The bot does not speak the text.
ttsPronounce.clearDesc: The broadcaster can use !tts pronounce clear to remove all entries for the channel. Built-in entries stay active.
ttsPronounce.notes: The word is not case-sensitive, and it must match a full word. A channel can have a maximum of 100 entries. A word can have a maximum of 40 characters. A spoken form can have a maximum of 120 characters. You can also change these entries in the Web Dashboard.

ttsProfanity.name: !tts profanity <block|allow|status>
ttsProfanity.description: Starts or stops the profanity filter, which replaces rude words with milder words.
ttsProfanity.statusNote: (shows the state, the language, and the number of words)
ttsProfanity.notes: The filter is off until you start it. It replaces rude words with milder words. It does not remove the message. The Banned Words list in the Web Dashboard removes a full message. The older words on and off still work: on is the same as block.

voices.title: Voices
voices.introText: The bot provides 472 voices across 45 languages from the MiniMax speech-2.8-turbo model. If the primary provider is unavailable, the bot falls back to speech-02-turbo. Use the voice_id in commands such as !tts voice <voice_id>.
voices.popularText: Popular voices from the MiniMax speech-2.8-turbo model. To select a voice, use !tts voice <voice_id> in chat.
voices.completeListTitle: Complete Voice List (from Wavespeed AI minimax/speech-02-turbo Schema — fallback provider)
voices.completeListText: This list contains all 472 available voices organized by language prefix.
voices.expandText: Select to expand complete voice list (472 voices across 45 languages)
voices.completeListNote: Note: The bot uses MiniMax speech-2.8-turbo with automatic fallback to speech-02-turbo. The list includes 472 voices categorized by language prefix. The command !tts voices links to this section.

languageBoost.title: Language Boost
languageBoost.introText: The language_boost feature improves pronunciation for specific languages and dialects. This setting helps in multilingual chats and non-English streams.
languageBoost.commandText: Set a personal language preference with !tts language <language_name>. Moderators can set a channel default with !tts defaultlanguage <language_name>.
languageBoost.usageText: The auto setting uses automatic language detection. For English chats, set English. Selecting a specific language improves pronunciation for that language.
languageBoost.announcementsText1: The channel language also selects the language of the text that the bot writes. This text includes stream event announcements, emote descriptions, and chat replies to commands.
languageBoost.announcementsText2: For example, a viewer subscribes to a Spanish channel. The bot then makes the announcement in Spanish.
languageBoost.announcementsText3: A personal language from !tts language changes the voice for your own messages only. A personal language does not change the announcements, because the whole channel hears them. The auto setting names no language, so a channel on auto gets announcements in English.
languageBoost.detectionText1: WildcatTTS reads the language that your channel declares on Twitch. The bot then sets the channel default for you.
languageBoost.detectionText2: The bot changes this setting only for a channel that has no language of its own. Your own choice always stays. Twitch has some languages that the voice engine does not support. For these languages, the channel stays on auto.

emoteDescriptions.title: Emote Descriptions
emoteDescriptions.introText: WildcatTTS uses Google Gemini AI to describe Twitch emotes in chat messages. Instead of reading the emote code (for example, "LUL"), TTS speaks a description such as "a person laughing." The bot caches descriptions permanently to prevent repeated AI requests.
emoteDescriptions.step1: When an emote appears for the first time, AI analyzes the emote image and creates a short description.
emoteDescriptions.step2: The bot caches the description permanently after first generation.
emoteDescriptions.step3: Later uses of the emote use the cached description instantly without new AI processing.
emoteDescriptions.managementText: Moderators can use !tts emote to view, regenerate, or set emote descriptions. See the Emote Description Management table for details.
emoteDescriptions.localeText: The AI writes each description in the language of the channel. The bot keeps a separate description for each language.

webDashboard.title: Web Dashboard
webDashboard.introText: The WildcatTTS Web Dashboard lets broadcasters configure all TTS settings. Sign in with your Twitch account to access the dashboard.
webDashboard.settingEngineDesc: Turn TTS on or off, announce stream events, and set TTS mode and permissions.
webDashboard.settingViewerDesc: Allow viewer custom voices, or force the channel default voice for all messages.
webDashboard.settingAllowPreferencesDesc: Allow viewers to choose custom voices with !myvoice, or lock TTS to the channel default voice.
webDashboard.settingBotChatDesc: Turn chat text replies on or off while keeping TTS voice audio active.
webDashboard.settingAnonymizeFollowersDesc: Announce new followers without speaking usernames for viewer privacy.
webDashboard.settingAnnounceCheersDesc: Turn cheer alerts on or off while continuing to read cheer messages.
webDashboard.settingAnnounceRedemptionsDesc: Turn channel point reward redemption alerts on or off.
webDashboard.settingAnnounceQueuedRedeemsDesc: Announce queued channel point rewards immediately without waiting for approval.
webDashboard.settingUrlDesc: Read full web links or only domain names.
webDashboard.settingBitsDesc: Announce cheers, read the message attached to a cheer, and set the minimum Bits a cheer needs.
webDashboard.settingChannelPointsDesc: Create and configure a custom Channel Point reward for TTS.
webDashboard.settingYoutubeDesc: Enable YouTube Live chat TTS and set your YouTube handle or stream URL.
webDashboard.settingIgnoreDesc: Manage the TTS ignore list, banned words, and pronunciation dictionary.
webDashboard.settingBannedWordsDesc: Block specific words or phrases so TTS skips matching messages.
webDashboard.settingVoiceDesc: Set channel defaults for voice, volume, emotion, pitch, speed, language, and text normalization.
webDashboard.settingObsDesc: Get your secure OBS browser source URL and setup instructions.
webDashboard.settingPreviewDesc: Test your voice settings before you go live.
webDashboard.obsStep1Title: Step 1: Add Browser Source in OBS
webDashboard.obsStep1_1: In OBS, click the "+" icon under Sources
webDashboard.obsConfigUrlDesc: Paste your copied OBS Browser Source URL from the dashboard
webDashboard.obsConfigControl: ✓ Control audio via OBS (must be checked)
webDashboard.obsConfigShutdown: Make sure that "Shutdown source when not visible" is unchecked so audio plays consistently
webDashboard.obsStep2_1: Locate the audio mixer in OBS (bottom panel)
webDashboard.obsStep2_2: Click the gear (⚙️) next to "Wildcat TTS" → "Advanced Audio Properties"
webDashboard.obsMonitorOutputDesc: - You and your stream hear the audio
webDashboard.obsMonitorOnlyDesc: - Only you hear the audio (for testing)
webDashboard.obsImportantDesc: Make sure that the source is unmuted in your audio mixer and the volume is set appropriately.
webDashboard.voiceCalibrationIntro: Some voices are naturally louder or quieter than other voices. Voice Calibration lets you set volume multipliers for individual voices to balance audio levels.
webDashboard.voiceCalibrationFeature1: Per-Voice Volume: Select a voice and assign a volume multiplier (0.1x to 10.0x). (Caution: Values over 1.0 can be loud)
webDashboard.voiceCalibrationFeature2: Auto-Apply: When a viewer selects a calibrated voice, the bot applies the custom volume automatically.
webDashboard.voiceCalibrationFeature3: Overrides: Calibrated voice volumes override the channel default volume setting.
webDashboard.settingCalibrationDesc: Set volume multipliers for individual voices to balance audio levels.
webDashboard.settingPageLanguageDesc: Select the language of the dashboard text. The selector is at the top of the page. This selector does not change the voice or the announcements.

troubleshooting.title: Troubleshooting
troubleshooting.a1: Make sure that the bot is a moderator in your channel. Type /mod WildcatTTS in your Twitch chat. The bot requires moderator permissions to read messages and send replies.
troubleshooting.a2: Make sure that TTS is enabled with !tts on in chat. Also check the active mode with !tts mode and permissions with !tts permission.
troubleshooting.q3: Bot not speaking in a specific language, or reading numbers in Chinese?
troubleshooting.a3: Set Language Boost to your language with !tts language <language_name> (or !tts defaultlanguage <language_name> for the channel). Show the active setting with !tts defaultlanguage.
troubleshooting.q4: TTS generation taking too long or failing?
troubleshooting.a4: The bot uses 302.ai with automatic fallback to Wavespeed AI. If audio delays occur, use !tts stop to cancel stuck generation. The bot retries failed requests automatically.
troubleshooting.a5: The auto emotion is not supported. Use neutral, happy, sad, angry, fearful, disgusted, or surprised.
troubleshooting.a6: Contact the developer through the contact form at Henry's portfolio website.

pronunciation.title: Pronunciation Dictionary
pronunciation.introText: Chat uses many short forms that TTS speaks one letter at a time. The pronunciation dictionary changes them into full words. For example, TTS speaks ngl as "not gonna lie" and glhf as "good luck have fun". WildcatTTS includes a built-in list of about 70 common short forms. You can also add your own entries.
pronunciation.rule1: The word is not case-sensitive. An entry for lfg also matches LFG.
pronunciation.rule2: An entry must match a full word. An entry for fr does not change the word "friend".
pronunciation.rule3: The dictionary does not change text inside a link.
pronunciation.rule4: The dictionary changes each word one time. TTS does not scan replaced text for more entries.
pronunciation.customText: Moderators can add entries with the !tts pronounce command or in the Web Dashboard. Custom entries are useful for channel names, game terms, and difficult words.
pronunciation.custom1: Your entry replaces a built-in entry with the same word.
pronunciation.custom2: To stop a built-in entry, use !tts pronounce off <word>. To restore it, use !tts pronounce remove <word>.
pronunciation.custom3: A channel can have a maximum of 100 entries.
pronunciation.switchText: The dictionary is active for all channels by default. To turn it off, turn off Expand Chat Acronyms in the Web Dashboard. TTS then speaks short forms letter by letter.
pronunciation.lolTip: TTS already speaks lol as "el oh el". This is standard behavior and requires no dictionary entry.
pronunciation.rule5: Some entries work in specific languages only. For example, the dictionary changes ty to "thank you" in English. In Polish, Czech, and Slovak, ty is a common word, so the dictionary keeps it.
pronunciation.custom4: A new entry of your own works in all languages. An entry that replaces a built-in entry keeps the languages of that built-in entry.

profanityFilter.title: Profanity Filter
profanityFilter.introText: The profanity filter replaces rude words with milder words before TTS speaks them. For example, TTS speaks "what the fuck" as "what the freak". The filter is off until a moderator turns it on.
profanityFilter.startText: Use !tts profanity block in chat, or turn on Profanity Filter in the Web Dashboard. Use !tts profanity status to see the current state, active language, and word count. Use !tts profanity allow to stop the filter again. The older words on and off still work.
profanityFilter.behavior1: The filter replaces rude words with milder words. The bot does not drop the message or play a bleep sound.
profanityFilter.behavior2: The filter replaces slurs with the word "slur" to remove offensive content from the audio.
profanityFilter.behavior3: The filter also applies to short forms from the pronunciation dictionary. When the filter is on, TTS speaks lfg as "let's freaking go".
profanityFilter.behavior4: Words must match fully. The filter does not modify words such as "class".
profanityFilter.languageText: The filter includes word lists for all 40 languages that Language Boost supports. The bot uses the word list for your channel language. If a viewer selects a personal language, the filter uses both lists. The English list is always active because the pronunciation dictionary is in English.
profanityFilter.languageAutoText: If Language Boost is set to "auto", the filter uses the English list. The bot cannot detect the language of every message.
profanityFilter.languageCoverageText: The English word list is the largest. Lists for other languages are smaller. Slurs exist only in the English list.
profanityFilter.bannedWordsTip: The profanity filter is different from Banned Words. Banned Words skips the entire message. The profanity filter speaks the message with milder words.

bannedWords.title: Banned Words
bannedWords.introText: The Banned Words feature stops WildcatTTS from speaking unwanted messages. If a chat message contains a banned word or phrase, TTS skips the message completely. The bot does not generate audio for skipped messages.
bannedWords.rule1: Matching is not case-sensitive. If you ban "badword", TTS also catches "BadWord" and "BADWORD".
bannedWords.rule2: TTS matches parts of words. If you ban "spam", TTS also skips messages that contain "spammer" or "spammy".
bannedWords.rule3: You can ban multi-word phrases. For example, you can ban phrases such as "follow my link" or "free followers".
bannedWords.rule4: TTS ignores the username in replies. If a reply mentions a user with a banned word in their name, TTS does not skip the message.
bannedWords.eventsIntro: The bot handles events and chat messages differently when a message contains a banned word:
bannedWords.eventChat: Chat Messages: TTS skips the full message. No voice audio plays.
bannedWords.eventResub: Resubscriptions: The bot announces the resubscription, but omits the attached viewer message.
bannedWords.eventStreak: Watch Streaks: The bot announces the streak count, but omits the attached viewer message.
bannedWords.eventRedemption: Channel Point Redemptions: The bot announces the reward redemption, but omits the custom text input.
bannedWords.eventRewardPolicy: Custom Reward Policy: If a Channel Point reward has a content policy, the bot rejects redemptions that contain banned words.
bannedWords.manageIntro: You can configure banned words in the Web Dashboard. Changes take effect immediately.
bannedWords.step1: Sign in to the Web Dashboard at tts.wildcat.chat with your Twitch account.
bannedWords.step2: Scroll to the Banned Words / Phrases card in the Ignored Users section.
bannedWords.step3: Type a word or phrase into the input field.
bannedWords.step4: Click Add, or press Enter on your keyboard.
bannedWords.step5: If you want to remove an entry, click Remove next to the word in the list.
bannedWords.comparisonTip: Banned Words skips the full message. The Profanity Filter speaks the message with milder words. If a message contains words on both lists, TTS skips the message.

youtubeTts.title: YouTube Live Chat Integration
youtubeTts.intro: WildcatTTS can read YouTube Live chat messages aloud into your OBS audio feed. If you stream to Twitch and YouTube at the same time, the bot reads messages from both chats into one audio source.
youtubeTts.feature1: Multi-streaming support: Messages from Twitch and YouTube play through the same OBS Browser Source without extra audio setup.
youtubeTts.feature2: Background polling: If you turn on the feature before you start your YouTube stream, the bot waits and connects when you go live.
youtubeTts.feature3: Heartbeat system: The bot sends regular heartbeat signals to keep the YouTube connection active during slow chat.
youtubeTts.feature4: Unified formatting: Custom YouTube emotes, URLs, and channel default voice settings apply to YouTube messages automatically.
youtubeTts.setupIntro: You can configure YouTube TTS in the Web Dashboard. Changes take effect immediately.
youtubeTts.step1: Sign in to the Web Dashboard at tts.wildcat.chat with your Twitch account.
youtubeTts.step2: Scroll to the YouTube Integration card.
youtubeTts.step3: Turn on the YouTube TTS Enabled switch.
youtubeTts.step5: If your stream is already live, OBS begins speaking your YouTube chat messages immediately.

urlReading.title: Speech-Friendly URL Reading
urlReading.intro: Chat messages often contain long web links with parameters and tracking codes. WildcatTTS simplifies links so they sound natural when spoken.
urlReading.rule1: By default, TTS replaces links with speech-friendly domain names. For example, TTS speaks a search link as "google dot com link".
urlReading.rule2: TTS removes protocol prefixes such as "https://" and "www." before speaking the domain name.
urlReading.rule3: TTS replaces hyphens, underscores, and dots with spaces and words so the domain sounds natural.
urlReading.toggleText: If you want TTS to speak entire URLs as typed, turn on the Read Full URLs switch in the Web Dashboard. When this switch is on, TTS speaks the full link without shortening.

eventControls.title: Stream Events & Privacy Controls
eventControls.intro: WildcatTTS gives you granular control over stream event announcements and viewer privacy in the Web Dashboard.
eventControls.cheersText: When a viewer cheers bits, TTS automatically strips cheermote names like Cheer100 or Party1 from the message. TTS only reads the viewer's custom message.
eventControls.cheersToggleText: Both switches are in the Cheers card of the Web Dashboard. Announce Cheers turns the "User cheered bits" alert on or off. Read Cheer Messages turns reading the attached message on or off. Cheer messages are read in every TTS mode and are not limited by TTS Permission, because the viewer paid for them.
eventControls.redemptionsText: When a viewer redeems a channel point reward, TTS speaks an alert with the reward title and the viewer message.
eventControls.redemptionsToggleText: Use the Announce Reward Redeems switch in the Web Dashboard to turn redemption alerts on or off.
eventControls.queuedRedeemsText: By default, the bot announces queued rewards only after you accept them in Twitch. Enable the Announce Queued Redeems Immediately switch to announce queued rewards immediately when redeemed.
eventControls.followersText: To protect viewer privacy, turn on the Anonymize New Followers switch in the Web Dashboard. When active, TTS announces "Someone new just followed!" instead of speaking the viewer's username.
eventControls.streaksText: When a viewer hits a watch streak milestone, the bot announces the streak count. If the viewer attached a message, the bot checks pronouns.alejo.io to speak their pronouns (for example, "They said: ...").
